REPORT
File No 1547
Date May 21, 1940

Subject Betty BIRNBAUM - suspected White Slave Trafficking

Made by D.P.S. Killingbeck Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

With reference to the cablegram which was
addressed to Betty BIRNBAUM through Box No.
1132 which is leased by Mr. R.C. FOWLES, this
cablegram was sent by Mr. FOWLES to Mr. P. KOMOR
for disposal.

As Betty BIRNBAUM was registered with the
I.C. Committee and her address was on record
on Committee files, Mr. KOMOR communicated
with the addressee and asked her to call at
his office to collect the cablegram.

On May 1, 1940, Betty BIRNBAUM called
at Mr. KOMOR's office personally and the
cablegram was handed over to her. Mr. KOMOR
asked her to explain why she had used Box No.
1132 and in explanation was told that a mistake
had probably been made as the address intended
was Box 1131, the Committee Box No. Betty
BIRNBAUM also explained that there was a slight
mistake made in the text of the cable and that
the word "MADELLE" should actually read "MODELLE".
This would change the literal meaning of the word
to "MODELS," instead of "GIRL" as translated by
Mr. KOMOR in his memorandum to D.S. Pitts. It
does not, however, appear to alter the general
meaning of the cablegram. Mr. KOMOR did not
ask for a full explanation from Betty BIRNBAUM
as he apparently did not wish to create the
impression that further enquiries would be made.

FILE
In.

(S.B.) SPECIAL BRANCH
DATE 8/5/40

报告
档案号 1547
日期 1940年5月21日

主题：Betty BIRNBAUM - 涉嫌白人奴隶贩卖

制作人：副督察长 Killingbeck 转呈人：D. I. Crawford

关于通过 R.C. FOWLES 先生租用的第 1132 号信箱发送给 Betty BIRNBAUM 的电报，该电报由 FOWLES 先生发送给 P. KOMOR 先生处理。

由于 Betty BIRNBAUM 已在国际委员会（I.C. Committee）登记，且其地址记录在委员会档案中，KOMOR 先生与收件人取得了联系，并请她到其办公室领取电报。

1940年5月1日，Betty BIRNBAUM 亲自前往 KOMOR 先生的办公室，电报被移交给她。KOMOR 先生询问她为何使用第 1132 号信箱，得到的解释是可能弄错了， intended 的地址应为第 1131 号信箱，即委员会的信箱。Betty BIRNBAUM 还解释说，电文中有轻微错误，“MADELLE”一词实际上应为“MODELLE”。这将把该词的字面意思从 KOMOR 先生在给 D.S. Pitts 的备忘录中翻译的“女孩”（GIRL）改为“模特”（MODELS）。然而，这似乎并未改变电报的总体含义。KOMOR 先生没有要求 Betty BIRNBAUM 做出全面解释，因为他显然不希望造成将进一步调查的印象。

归档
入档
1942年5月2日

Made by D.P.S. Killingbeck.    Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

In connection with previous reports on
above, D.P.S. Killingbeck and D.P.S. Yoshinaga
furnished necessary particulars regarding the time
and date on which the cablegram was despatched by
Betty BIRNBAUM, to Mr. T. Matsusaki and the Director
of Central China Tele-Communication Corporation, on
May 3, 1940.

Mr. Matsusaki promised to have the
cablegram traced and a copy forwarded to Police
Headquarters. He later communicated with D.P.S.
Yoshinaga and requested that an official letter be
addressed to the company by the S.M.P., requesting
particulars of the cablegram.

C.D.I. Nakamura was informed of this by
D.P.S. Yoshinaga but up to the present nothing
further has been heard of the matter.

Mr. Fowles has been informed that the
Refugee Committee P.O. Box No. is the next to his
own and that it is quite possible that a mistake was
made in addressing letters. No further instances
have occurred.

Killingbeck.
D. F. S.

D. C. ( Special Branch ).

鉴于上述之前的报告，副督察长 Killingbeck 和副督察长 Yoshinaga 于 1940年5月3日向 T. Matsusaki 先生及华中电信公司总经理提供了关于 Betty BIRNBAUM 发出电报的时间和日期的必要细节。

Matsusaki 先生承诺追踪该电报并将副本发送至警察总局。他后来与副督察长 Yoshinaga 联系，要求工部局警务处向该公司发出一封正式信函，索取电报详情。

副督察长 Yoshinaga 将此情况告知了刑事侦缉督察 Nakamura，但截至目前，此事再无下文。

已告知 Fowles 先生，难民委员会的邮政信箱号码紧邻他的信箱，因此在投递信件时很有可能发生错误。此后未再发生类似情况。

Killingbeck.
D. F. S.

Special Branch D.S. Section LL
REPORT
Date April 30, 1940

Subject Betty BIRBAUM - suspected White Slave trafficking.

Made by D. S. Pitts Forwarded by D.I. Crawford.

The attached memorandum was received by D.S.
Pitts during the afternoon of April 30, 1940 from
Mr. KOMOR, Hon. Secretary of the I.C. Committee.
The cablegram to which this memorandum refers was
addressed to P.O. Box 1132, which is rented by
R.C. Fowles, 154 Nanking Road. According to Mr.
Komor, Mr. Fowles states that his Box has been
utilized on several occasions by European refugees
for the receipt of mail and bable matter without
his permission.

The last word "emes" in the original of the
cable, which is now in the possession of Mr.
Komor, having been handed over to him by Mr.
Fowles, is a Hebrew slang expression used by
criminal elements.

Betty BIRBAUM, the addressee, has made a
number of trips recently between Shanghai and Harbin
but her present local address is not known. Mr.
KOMOR has advertised in the refugee press to the
effect that a cable is awaiting her at the I.C.
office; it will be handed her on her personal
appearance.

（签名）
J. Sikes.
D. S.

D. C. (Special Branch).

D. S. Pitts
（批注符号）

日期 1940年4月30日

主题 Betty BIRBAUM - 涉嫌白人奴隶贩卖。

制作人：D. S. Pitts 转呈人：D.I. Crawford。

D.S. Pitts 于 1940年4月30日下午收到国际委员会荣誉秘书 KOMOR 先生提交的附函备忘录。该备忘录所指的电报寄往第 1132 号邮政信箱，该信箱由南京路 154 号的 R.C. Fowles 租用。据 Komor 先生称，Fowles 先生表示，他的信箱曾多次被欧洲难民未经许可用于接收邮件和电报业务。

目前由 Komor 先生持有的电报原件（由 Fowles 先生移交给他），其最后一个词“emes”是犯罪团伙使用的希伯来语俚语表达。

收件人 Betty BIRBAUM 最近多次往返于上海和哈尔滨之间，但其目前的本地地址不详。KOMOR 先生已在难民报刊上刊登广告，称有一份电报在国际委员会办公室等候她；待其亲自现身时将予以交付。

（签名）
J. Sikes.
D. S.

D. C. (特别处)。

D. S. Pitts
（批注符号）

applicable to it in his personal custody.

        遵照 Toon 巡官（犯罪科副总监助理）的指示，下述签署人于 1940年5月1日下午 4:30 前往沙逊大厦的华中电信公司，采访了总务部经理 T. Matsusaki 先生，并要求他提供据信以 BETTY BIRNBAUM 之名通过该公司发送和接收的电报详情。他表示愿意提供协助，但指出由于以下原因，这样做相当困难：-
    1) 首先，需要确认接收发给 Betty Birnbaum 的电报的具体办事处名称。否则，无法核查收到的电报。
    2) 至于那些可能由 Betty Birnbaum 发往哈尔滨的电报，希望能告知大致日期。
        为了让下述签署人满意，Matsusaki 先生带领下述签署人前往通信控制室，并核查了频繁使用者的名单，但未找到 Betty Birnbaum 这个名字。
        他还表示，附件报告中提到的第 1132 号邮政信箱能被他人使用是很奇怪的，因为常识而言，除了租用该信箱并应亲自保管相应钥匙的人之外，任何人无法打开该信箱。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No.__________
C. B. HEADQUARTERS Station,
REPORT
Date May 2nd, 1940.

Subject BETTY BIRNBAUM- suspected White slave trafficking.
-2-
Made by D.P.S. Yoshinaga. Forwarded by C.D.I. Nakamura.

Acting on instructions from Supt. Toon,
P.A. to D.C.Crime, the undersigned proceeded, at 4.30
P.M. on the 1-5-40, to the Central China Tele-communi-
cation Corporation, Sassoon House and interviewed
Mr. T. Matsusaki, i/c the General Affairs Dept. and
requested him to furnish us particulars of cablegrams
believed to have been despatched and received through
the medium of the concern in the name of one BETTY
BIRNBAUM. He stated that he was prepared to give
assistance but pointed out it was rather difficult to
do so from the following reasons:-
1) First of all, it is desired that the name of
the office via which cablegrams addressed to Betty
Birnbaum were received be confirmed. Otherwise, it is
impossible to check up the cablegrams received.
2) As for those which might have been despatched
by Betty Birnbaum to Harbin, it is hoped that the
approximate dates be informed.
To satisfy the undersigned, Mr. Matsusaki
led the undersigned to the Communication Control Room
and checked up the names of frequent users but no such
name as Betty Birnbaum could be found.
He further stated it is strange that the P.O.
Box 1132 referred to in the attached report could be
utilized by others whereas, as a matter of common-sense,
the box cannot be opened by anyone except by the person
who has rented it and who should have kept the key
applicable to it in his personal custody.
